definition: Automated machine learning (AutoML) is the process of automating the tasks of applying machine learning to real-world problems.
details: It is the combination of automation and ML. AutoML potentially includes every stage from beginning with a raw dataset to building a machine learning model ready for deployment. AutoML was proposed as an artificial intelligence-based solution to the growing challenge of applying machine learning. The high degree of automation in AutoML aims to allow non-experts to make use of machine learning models and techniques without requiring them to become experts in machine learning. Automating the process of applying machine learning end-to-end additionally offers the advantages of producing simpler solutions, faster creation of those solutions, and models that often outperform hand-designed models. Common techniques used in AutoML include hyperparameter optimization, meta-learning and neural architecture search.

explainer.lead: Automated machine learning, or AutoML, uses automation to handle the work involved in turning a machine-learning problem into a usable model. It can make these techniques accessible to non-experts while also helping produce solutions more quickly.

tiers.eli5: Building a machine-learning model can be like trying many recipes and oven settings to find one that works well. AutoML is a helper that tries many of those choices for you, starting with the ingredients and working toward a finished result. This means you can use machine learning without first becoming an expert.
tiers.practitioner: AutoML can automate stages from a raw dataset through to a model ready for deployment, using techniques such as hyperparameter optimization, meta-learning, and neural architecture search. It is useful for reducing manual design and tuning work, but automation should not be read as a guarantee that every resulting model will outperform a hand-designed one.
tiers.paperLevel: In plain-text notation, AutoML can be viewed as AutoML(D, task) -> M, where D is a raw dataset and M is a model ready for deployment. Its scope can include hyperparameter optimization, meta-learning, and neural architecture search, with the goals of simpler solutions, faster creation, and models that often outperform hand-designed models.

explainer.example: A team provides a raw table of customer records and wants a model that predicts customer churn. Instead of manually tuning every modeling choice, it uses AutoML to optimize settings and search model designs, ending with a model ready for deployment.

explainer.intuition: Applying machine learning involves many design and tuning decisions. AutoML treats those decisions as tasks that can be automated, rather than requiring a person to make each one by hand.
howItWorks: Begin with a real-world problem and, potentially, a raw dataset.
Apply automation across stages of the machine-learning process.
Use techniques such as hyperparameter optimization, meta-learning, or neural architecture search to make modeling choices.
Produce a machine-learning model ready for deployment.
explainer.whyItMatters: AutoML addresses the growing challenge of applying machine learning by reducing the expertise and manual work required. Its end-to-end automation can produce simpler solutions, create them faster, and often yield models that outperform hand-designed ones.
misconceptions: AutoML is not just hyperparameter optimization; it can potentially cover every stage from a raw dataset to deployment.
Models produced by AutoML often outperform hand-designed models, but that is not a guarantee in every case.
AutoML is not one single technique; common techniques within it include hyperparameter optimization, meta-learning, and neural architecture search.
